intro: Searching for insurance advisers near you usually means you want someone local who can help you make sense of cover for your home, your business or your family's protection. You may be comparing a few options or simply want a straightforward conversation about what you need. iComply introduces you to a suitable UK insurance broker who can quote you directly.
need_heading: What people looking for insurance advisers nearby often need
need_lead: Most people searching for insurance advisers near me want practical help choosing cover that fits their situation, not a sales pitch.
needs: You have a home, a flat or a rental property and want to be sure the buildings and contents cover is right for what you own.
You run a small business and need to understand which risks you are required to insure and which ones you should consider.
You are self-employed or have a family and want to look at protection such as life cover or income protection.
You have a policy already but are unsure what is excluded or whether it still suits your circumstances.
You want to compare quotes from a few different insurers but would rather talk it through with someone local first.
context_heading: Understanding how insurance advice works in the UK
context: Insurance brokers and intermediaries in the UK must be authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority, or be appointed representatives of an authorised firm. You can check any adviser on the FCA register before you speak to them. Many brokers also belong to the British Insurance Brokers' Association, and some hold Chartered status from the Chartered Insurance Institute.

A broker must understand your demands and needs, explain the key features and exclusions of a policy, and tell you how they are paid. If a complaint is not resolved, you can take it to the Financial Ombudsman Service. iComply is not regulated and does not give advice; we simply introduce you to a professional who can.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Say what you want cover for, such as your home, your business or your family's protection.
Mention whether you already have a policy and when it is due for renewal.
Describe any particular concerns, such as a high-value item, a listed building or a business activity that might need specialist cover.
Let us know your rough budget range so the broker can suggest suitable options.
Confirm that you would like to speak to someone local to you, and give your area or postcode.
Add anything else that affects your risk, such as whether you work from home or have employees.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the insurance adviser
questions: Are you authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority, and can you give me your firm reference number?
How do you get paid for arranging my cover, and will you tell me in writing?
What are the main exclusions in the policies you are recommending for my situation?
Will you explain my demands and needs and confirm that the cover matches them?
What support will you give me if I need to make a claim?
Are you a member of the British Insurance Brokers' Association or a Chartered firm?

faqs.q: How do I check that an insurance adviser is properly authorised?
faqs.a: You can search the Financial Conduct Authority's register online for the firm's name or reference number. This will show whether they are authorised or an appointed representative. It is a quick and free check you can do before you speak to them.

faqs.q: What is the difference between an insurance broker and an insurance company?
faqs.a: An insurance broker acts for you, helping you understand your needs and comparing policies from different insurers. An insurance company provides the policy itself. Brokers must explain how they are paid and whose interests they represent.

faqs.q: Will an insurance adviser near me always find me the cheapest cover?
faqs.a: Not necessarily, and it is not always the right goal. The cheapest policy may have exclusions that leave you underinsured. A good adviser will focus on matching cover to your needs and explaining the trade-offs so you can judge for yourself.

faqs.q: What can I do if I am unhappy with the advice I receive?
faqs.a: First raise your complaint with the firm directly. If it is not resolved to your satisfaction, you can take it to the Financial Ombudsman Service, which is free for consumers. The firm should tell you how to do this.
